data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The single best cross-city modulator is wind speed: on calm nights the nocturnal UHI is maximized because turbulent mixing is suppressed, and cities with climatologically lower wind speeds or deeper street canyons that shelter the surface from wind exhibit a larger night-time gap.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If nocturnal UHI magnitude is uncorrelated with wind speed across cities after controlling for other factors, this mechanism fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the UHI is large even on windy nights in some cities, wind sheltering is insufficient.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If building height increases but wind speed does not decrease within canyons, the sheltering mechanism is unsupported.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Wind speed controls the rate at which urban heat is ventilated away. On clear, calm nights, reduced wind speed in urban canyons traps sensible heat released from thermal storage. The cross-city magnitude of the nocturnal UHI scales inversely with wind speed and positively with building height, because deeper canyons reduce effective ventilation. Cities with lower wind speeds or denser geometry thus maintain a larger nighttime temperature excess.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
